task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 (regression test) for ISS-0119. Build the two test files the design specifies and PERFORM the fail-first demonstration. §7 gives assertions A0-A8, §7.1 gives the required procedure and the four outputs you must quote, §8 gives the digest definition.

CREATE: test/support/status_history.ex (module Letflow.Test.StatusHistory, six functions plus current_volume/2 and default_ceilings/0, signatures in §7), test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs (assertions A0-A8), test/specs/ISS-0119.md (the test spec, carrying the fail-first evidence). ELIXIR-DEV deliberately did NOT create the two test files -- they are yours. mix.exs:20 already puts test/support on the :test load path, verified independently by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and REVIEWER at both HEAD and the pre-fix commit, so no build-config change is needed.

=== THREE CONDITIONS CARRIED FROM REVIEWER'S STEP 3D RULING, all binding ===

C1 -- APPLY THE §8 ERRATUM AND USE THE CORRECTED FORM. ELIXIR-DEV found, and REVIEWER independently reproduced, that §8's THREE digest implementations do not agree as §8 claims. Bash normative and PowerShell both yield 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804 (355,610 bytes hashed). §8's ELIXIR form as written yields 5c9fda42d72b0d46e4bf60cfc5a0fc044d7c36eb0192bc4b5e599c2a559b657a (361,376 bytes) -- exactly +5,766, one byte per line. Cause: File.stream!/1 opens in TEXT MODE on a CRLF checkout and has already stripped the CR, so String.trim_trailing(&1, "\r\n") -- which trims only that exact two-byte suffix -- matches nothing, the surviving \n stays, and <> "\n" appends a second. REVIEWER confirmed the mechanism directly: File.stream! yields line 1 as "# RoCo — Requirement run history\n", a bare \n. USE THIS CORRECTED FORM, which REVIEWER verified reproduces the normative value:

  File.stream!(path) |> Enum.take(n) |> Enum.map_join("", &((&1 |> String.trim_trailing("\n") |> String.trim_trailing("\r")) <> "\n")) |> then(&:crypto.hash(:sha256, &1)) |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: trim "\n" FIRST, then "\r"; never the literal two-byte "\r\n". This is what makes it correct on both a CRLF text-mode read and an LF/binary read, i.e. portable to CI where the checkout is LF. Quote the digest your test ACTUALLY computes and state whether it equals 5a1a64ab...804 -- §8's CHECK 5 was never dischargeable at Step 3 because the test did not exist yet, and ELIXIR-DEV correctly said so rather than claiming it.

C2 -- CORRECT §8 INLINE, in the same commit, marked as an erratum ruled at Step 3d. REVIEWER's reason is exactly this run's own subject matter: an erratum that lives only in a handoff is the 'recorded where nobody lands' failure ISS-0119 is about. You are explicitly authorized to edit lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md for THIS ONE CORRECTION ONLY -- §8's Elixir bullet and any sentence claiming the three forms agree. Change nothing else in the artefact; it passed a hard gate on its third pass and the rest of it is not yours to revise.

C3 -- ONE ExUnit `test` BLOCK PER ASSERTION. A0 through A8 each get their own block. This is not style: ExUnit aborts a block at its first failed assertion, and A0 is EXPECTED to fail in the pre-fix run (no index exists there). If A0 and A3 shared a block with A0 first, A3 would never execute and the pre-fix run would short-circuit on the missing index -- resurrecting the precise failure §7.1 opens by rejecting, and destroying the fail-first proof. A3 must not be preceded by A0 in the same block. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR raised this as MINOR M1, ELIXIR-DEV confirmed §7's flat-bullet wording permits the bad reading, and REVIEWER concurred.

=== THE FAIL-FIRST DEMONSTRATION IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL ===

§7.1 is explicit that this obligation must be PERFORMED, not declared satisfied. Run its procedure in a THROWAWAY GIT WORKTREE against pre-fix commit 3d19e8c -- never a `git checkout` in this checkout, which holds local main and has a live sibling worktree; CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR verified the worktree approach disturbs neither. Quote all four required outputs from §7.1 VERBATIM, no paraphrase, and state plainly that A0 is expected to fail in that same pre-fix run for the same reason so no reader is misled by two red assertions. Clean up the throwaway worktree when done.

The property that must be demonstrated: A3 fails pre-fix ON SIZE (over: [:lines, :bytes], ~4,217 lines / ~260,644 bytes) via the {:no_index_fallback, "docs/status/requirement_status.yaml"} resolution -- NOT on a missing file -- and passes post-fix because the current volume resolves through the index to v2. If what you actually observe differs from that table in any way, report it; do not adjust the test until it produces the expected story.

=== SCOPE ===

Do NOT run the full suite -- TEST-RUNNER owns that at Step 4c, and REVIEWER noted the project gate is currently RED for pre-existing reasons unrelated to this branch (ISS-0109/ISS-0116 class). Running your own new test file, and the pre-fix worktree run, is required and expected. Do not touch docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, its volumes, the index, or any file under handoffs/ or test/reports/. handoffs/orchestrator.log has uncommitted ORCH edits -- leave it, stage by explicit path, never `git add -A`.

ONE THING REVIEWER ASKED BE PASSED ON: the moment you add these .exs files, this branch stops being a zero-code change, so REVIEWER's proof that the branch adds no failure main lacks EXPIRES. Do not restate that proof as though it still holds; TEST-RUNNER re-establishes the baseline independently at Step 4c.
acceptance_criteria: test/support/status_history.ex created per §7's signatures, with no function hardcoding the index location
test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs created with assertions A0 through A8, each in its own ExUnit test block (C3)
The §8 Elixir digest erratum is applied using REVIEWER's corrected form, trimming \n before \r (C1)
lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md §8 is corrected inline and marked as an erratum ruled at Step 3d, with nothing else in the artefact changed (C2)
The digest the test actually computes is quoted, and its equality or inequality with 5a1a64ab...804 is stated explicitly
The §7.1 fail-first procedure was PERFORMED in a throwaway worktree against 3d19e8c, and all four required outputs are quoted verbatim in test/specs/ISS-0119.md
The spec states A3 failed pre-fix on SIZE via the no_index_fallback resolution, not on a missing file, and notes A0 is expected to fail in the same run
The post-fix run of the same unmodified assertion passes, and its output is quoted
No file under docs/status/, handoffs/ or test/reports/ was modified, and handoffs/orchestrator.log was not committed

result.summary: All three test artefacts are built and all ten acceptance criteria are met; the fail-first demonstration was PERFORMED, not declared. test/support/status_history.ex implements every §7 signature (parse_index/1, measure/1, within_bounds?/3, entries/1, anomalies/3, frozen_prefix_digest/2, default_ceilings/0, current_volume/2, plus closure_footer/1, header/1 and entry_field_order/0 for A7/A8/A4) with no function hardcoding the index location or a volume list. test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs carries A0-A8 plus A3b, ONE test block each per C3, formatted clean and compiling with zero warnings. C1: the corrected digest form (trim "\n" then "\r", never the two-byte "\r\n") computes 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804 on this CRLF working tree -- EQUAL to the normative Bash value and to the index's frozen_prefix_sha256; §8 CHECK 5 is now discharged (A6 green). C2: §8 corrected inline with a marked erratum ruled at Step 3d; nothing else in the artefact touched. FAIL-FIRST: throwaway worktree at 3d19e8c (never a git checkout; sibling worktree letflow-wt2 undisturbed), two files copied in unmodified, mix deps.get, mix test. A3 failed pre-fix ON SIZE -- resolution {:no_index_fallback, "docs/status/requirement_status.yaml"}, over: [:lines, :bytes], 4,217 lines / 264,861 working-tree bytes (260,644 in the blob) against 1,200/120,000 -- NOT on a missing file. A0 failed in the same run for exactly that reason and the spec says so plainly. Post-fix, the same unmodified file gives 9/10 passed with A3 and A0 both green. Worktree removed and verified gone. All four §7.1 outputs are quoted verbatim in test/specs/ISS-0119.md. Status is PARTIAL, not PASS, for two honest reasons reported rather than tuned away: (1) A4 is RED on the fix branch on a REAL finding -- three previously undeclared malformed entries in frozen volume 1 -- and cannot be closed by TEST-DESIGNER; (2) the pre-fix run produced ten red assertions, not the two §7.1's prose anticipates. Both are detailed below and in test/specs/ISS-0119.md §6 and §4.

issues.description: A4 IS RED ON THE FIX BRANCH -- a real undeclared-drift finding, not a broken test, and TEST-DESIGNER cannot close it. Implemented exactly as §7 specifies ('every entry carries all five fields in order with a parseable ISO-8601 at:. Exceptions only as declared in A5'), A4 found three previously unknown malformed entries in volume 1 on its first ever run: line 4803 (REQ-053, started) has no note: field; line 4896 (REQ-056, started) names its timestamp field `timestamp:` instead of `at:`; line 5050 (REQ-054, started) has no note: field. Independently corroborated by grep -c over volume 1: 182 `- req:`, 182 `event:`, 182 `agent:`, but only 181 `at:` and 180 `note:` -- arithmetic matching those three exactly. Vocabulary is clean (A5 green, A4's vocabulary limb empty); these are SHAPE violations. Why not fixed here: (a) remediation lives in docs/status/, which this step is forbidden to touch, and the entries themselves must never be edited -- volume 1 is frozen and pinned by A6, so correcting them is the rewrite the append-only rule forbids; (b) the index has NO declaration mechanism for shape violations -- known_anomalies: is keyed {path,line,field,value} and A5 asserts it equals the on-disk VOCABULARY violation set exactly in both directions, so adding the three there would turn A5 red. Closing this needs a design amendment (e.g. a separate known_shape_anomalies: key that A4 subtracts and A5 ignores), which is CODE-DESIGNER/REVIEWER's call -- and this step was authorized to edit only §8 of an artefact that cleared a hard gate on its third pass. The test was deliberately NOT weakened: suppressing this would produce a test that only ever runs against already-correct code, and this is exactly the silent drift ISS-0119 exists to stop -- it accumulated for months with no mechanical check and the first mechanical check found it.

OBSERVED DIVERGENCE FROM DESIGN §7.1's PROSE, reported per instruction rather than tuned away. §7.1 anticipates 'two red assertions' in the pre-fix run. In fact ALL TEN were red: 'Result: 0/10 passed / Failed: 10 tests'. A0 and A3 failed as designed and are quoted verbatim in the spec; the other eight (A1, A2, A3b, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8) each raised '** (File.Error) could not read file "docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml": no such file or directory' -- because, exactly as §7.1's own opening paragraph states, every assertion except A3 is derived from an index that does not exist pre-fix, and only A3 was engineered to degrade. This is an oversight in §7.1's prose, not a defect in the test or the design's mechanism: the fail-first property §7.1 specifies holds precisely as written, with A3 failing on SIZE via the degraded resolution and not on a missing file. The test was NOT adjusted to produce a tidier story. No design edit was made for this, since C2 authorizes editing §8 only.

A1's literal wording in §7 ('every file matching docs/status/requirement_status*.yaml on disk appears in volumes:') would be self-failing, because that glob also matches docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml, which is the index and not a volume. The test excludes the index by its own exact path (never by a naming heuristic) with an inline comment saying why. Recorded so the deviation is visible rather than silent.

REVIEWER's Step 3d proof that this branch adds no failure main lacks HAS EXPIRED, as REVIEWER asked be passed on. It held while the branch was a zero-code change; these .ex/.exs files end that. It is not restated anywhere in the spec as though it still holds. TEST-RUNNER must re-establish the baseline independently at Step 4c. The full suite was deliberately NOT run here (Step 4c owns it); what was run is this one test file on the fix branch and in the pre-fix worktree.

result.next_action: ORCH: route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 4b) as normal, but rule first on the MAJOR above. A4 is red on the fix branch on a genuine finding that TEST-DESIGNER is not authorized to close -- three undeclared shape anomalies in frozen volume 1, and no index/design mechanism exists to declare them without breaking A5. This needs a design amendment from CODE-DESIGNER with REVIEWER sign-off (suggested: a known_shape_anomalies: key in the index that A4 subtracts and A5 ignores), plus the corresponding index edit by ELIXIR-DEV/DOC-UPDATER, before TEST-RUNNER's Step 4c gate can go green on this file. Everything else in Step 4 is complete: 9/10 assertions green post-fix, fail-first performed and quoted, §8 erratum applied and the digest confirmed equal to 5a1a64ab...804, worktree torn down.
